source.title: Adversarial Attacks Leverage Interference Between Features in Superposition
source.authors: Edward Stevinson; Lucas Prieto; Melih Barsbey; Tolga Birdal

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. The extracted text has some flattened tables and figure references, but it is not cut off or unusable.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether feature interference in superposed representations predicts adversarial perturbations, using bottleneck networks, image classifiers, and attack-geometry measures rather than reproducing the original toy-model method.
record.gate_note: Rows cover measured alignment with theoretical attack directions, geometry similarity across data-correlation conditions, attack transfer, ViT latent/input attack-profile correlations, and robustness as bottleneck pressure changes. The paper also reports SAE feature visualizations, but the supplied text gives no interpretable results from those figures; SAE reconstruction checks concern classifier accuracy and attack preservation, not whether SAE features are canonical or complete units.
record.test_reason: The paper mainly uses superposition to explain adversarial vulnerability. It also reports results on superposition geometry in a new toy setting (an argmax bottleneck classifier). With k>m, class vectors are non-orthogonal. At m=k they become orthogonal (Sec 4.4), and input correlations shape the arrangement (Sec 4.2, Table 6, Fig 2). This bears narrowly on V1. Most rows measure adversarial-attack properties, a related but different construct.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that superposition is sufficient but not necessary for adversarial vulnerability. In their account, input correlations (and, they say, sparsity) shape superposition geometry, and its interference patterns predict attack structure and transfer in toy models and ViTs. They present this as complementary to existing explanations. Note that sparsity was not actually varied in the experiments.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a synthetic argmax classification bottleneck and image-classifier bottlenecks to connect feature interference to adversarial attacks, rather than reproducing the original toy-model superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Synthetic geometry and transfer vary with input-correlation regime. In ViTs, latent/input attack-profile correlation generally falls as bottleneck dimension increases; in the no-explicit-bottleneck experiment it rises with weight decay and falling effective dimension.

fits_no_version.finding: PGD perturbations align with the interference-derived optimal direction (cos 0.92-0.97; random 0.00), in linear and ReLU variants. SPSA/Square alignment is 0.55-0.99 (Table 8).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adversarial perturbations exploit interference between superposed features.

fits_no_version.finding: Attack transfer rises from 5% to 98% as cross-seed geometric similarity increases with input correlation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Shared superposition geometry predicts adversarial transferability.

fits_no_version.finding: In ViT bottleneck heads, latent-profile/input-profile correlation ρ̄ rises as m/k or effective rank falls. The trend replicates in ResNet-50 and MLP-Mixer (Tables 11-12).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Interference in compressed classification heads predicts attack structure in realistic image models.

fits_no_version.finding: Robust accuracy falls monotonically with k/m at fixed m. There are no adversarial examples at m=k.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Superposition pressure is sufficient for adversarial vulnerability.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The central toy-model results use a simplified classification task; the authors say superposition is sufficient but not necessary. The text does not report a direct sweep over feature activation sparsity or feature importance. Image-model geometry is measured at the classification head, not across intermediate features. The SAE feature analyses are explicitly preliminary, and their figure-only outcomes are not described in the supplied text. The global-correlation transfer uncertainty is inconsistent between Section 4.3 and Figure 2.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit. Appendix Table 3 interference magnitude and cross-seed consistency metrics were not extracted because the attack-profile, geometry-similarity, and bottleneck results already capture the directly relevant outcomes. Appendix Table 13 SAE insertion accuracy was not included because it measures classifier behavior through SAE reconstruction, not the claim versions' representation-unit properties.

untested.parts: No sweep of feature sparsity or sparsity-dependent phase transition. No feature-importance variation. No test of regular polytope geometry: the cross-seed metric cannot show regularity. Features are class readout directions in a classification task, not sparse features reconstructed by an autoencoder.
Not tested: no neuron-level polysemanticity or importance-based allocation.
Not tested. The SAE appendix on CLIP-ViT is exploratory and gives figure-only outcomes. Table 13 checks only accuracy with the SAE inserted.
Not tested: no completeness, stability or canonicity analysis of SAE features.
Not tested: all features are assumed to be 1-D directions.

missing.what: Statement that at m=k the network learns orthogonal class vectors, versus non-orthogonal vectors for k>m.

Fig 2 geometric similarity for k=7, m=2 (0.01±0.20, 0.43±0.20, 0.97±0.01), and the qualitative arrangements: arbitrary angles when uncorrelated, paired features orthogonal, cyclic ordering under global correlation.
After fine-tuning a pretrained ViT, the bottleneck geometry shows approximately equal spacing (neural-collapse-like) with random ordering across seeds.
Interference magnitude I falls as m/k rises in ViT (e.g. CIFAR-10 0.61 to 0.12). The same trend appears in ResNet-50 and MLP-Mixer.
missing.versions: V1 (only analogically; these are not small networks)

missing.what: Adversarial accuracy stays low across bottlenecks while corruption accuracy tracks clean accuracy.

record.verdict_notes: Most results are adversarial-robustness measures that presuppose superposition, so they are moved to fits_no_version. Only a thin V1 geometry signal remains, mostly qualitative and largely by construction of the bottleneck. Fig 2's 'arbitrary angles across seeds' for uncorrelated data is ambiguous about regularity: the metric is label-specific. Neither it nor Table 6 should be read as challenging V1's regular geometry.

versions.untested_parts: Tests interference and geometry under sparse synthetic inputs, correlation regimes, and bottlenecks, and tests related attack-geometry effects in image classifiers. It does not sweep feature activation sparsity directly, test importance-dependent allocation of dimensions, or establish the original toy-model transition and regular geometry in full.
No test of neuron polysemanticity, importance-based dedication of dimensions, or lower-importance features sharing dimensions.
No test of whether polysemantic neurons arise without capacity pressure.
The SAE appendix concerns a vision model and gives exploratory figure descriptions, not a reported test of feature spreading across neurons or recoverability of LLM features.
No test of whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Uses class-level directions in its analysis but does not compare one-dimensional directions with multidimensional features.

relationships.condition: Linear (and ReLU-decoder) argmax bottleneck networks, k>m versus m=k
relationships.reason: Based on the text, not rows. Class vectors are non-orthogonal when k>m and become orthogonal at m=k (Sec 4.4, Fig 2). Paired correlations make paired features orthogonal (Fig 2), matching the toy-model correlated-feature result. Recorded in missing; R7-R15 cannot show regularity.
relationships.display_finding: Class vectors were non-orthogonal when k>m and became orthogonal at m=k, and paired correlations made the paired features orthogonal, matching the toy-model result for correlated features. Whether the geometry is regular was not shown.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Synthetic argmax models with bottlenecks; global input correlations; bottleneck ViTs on the tested image datasets
reader_labels.reason: PGD directions align with the interference-derived optimum, geometry and transfer vary with correlation structure, and image-model attack profiles track latent interference (R1-R3, R13-R15, R18-R34, R49-R50).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Uncorrelated or paired synthetic inputs; relaxed bottlenecks and non-bottleneck regularization settings
reader_labels.reason: Geometry is not consistently shared for uncorrelated data, is only partly constrained for paired data, and attack-profile alignment weakens as the bottleneck relaxes; the paper also frames superposition as sufficient but not necessary (R7-R12, R16-R17, R22, R26, R30, R34, R43-R48).
